en: The kind of spaces we study might best be described as “cultural zones.”66 Such zones exist, almost by definition, in the plural: to a large degree, they are defined relative to and in distinction from one another. Our project requires us to identify these zones spatially and conceptually, but also to reflect on their interactions.
zh: 我们研究的这类空间最好被描述为“文化区域”。66 这种区域几乎按定义就是复数：在很大程度上，它们是通过相对与区别来定义的。我们的项目要求我们在空间和概念上识别这些区域，同时也要思考它们之间的互动关系。

en: Stein entered Chinese territory on 29 May 1906 and arrived at Kashgar on 8 June 1906. With the assistance of George Macartney, British Political Agent at Kashgar, Stein engaged Jiang Xiaowan 蒋孝琬 (Chiang Ssŭ-yeh [Jiang shiye] 蒋师爷) from Yarkand as his Chinese secretary. An educated man, Jiang Xiaowan had been private secretary (Ssŭ-yeh) to several officials in Gansu and Xinjiang since 1883 but felt rather disappointed with his career. He thought Fortune was smiling on him when he was engaged by Stein. In the course of the next two years, Jiang Xiaowan helped Stein with all his heart and all his might. When one speaks of Stein’s dealings with Wang Yuanlu and Chinese officials, it would be more accurate to call them Jiang Xiaowan’s dealings with Wang Yuanlu and Chinese officials on behalf of Stein.7
zh: 斯坦因于1906年5月29日进入中国境内，6月8日抵达喀什。在英国驻喀什政治代表George Macartney的协助下，他从叶尔羌聘请蒋孝琬（Chiang Ssŭ-yeh，即蒋师爷）担任中文秘书。蒋孝琬受过教育，自1883年起曾为甘肃、新疆的多名官员担任私人幕僚（师爷），但对自己的仕途颇感失望。因此，获斯坦因聘用时，他以为时来运转。此后两年，蒋孝琬竭尽全力协助斯坦因。人们谈到斯坦因与王圆箓及中国官员的交涉时，更准确的说法应是：蒋孝琬代表斯坦因，与王圆箓及中国官员交涉。〔7〕

en: Concerned that the promise of money might not overcome the religious scruples and fear of popular resentment that Stein believed motivated Wang Yuanlu’s reluctance, he decided to pay him a formal visit.80 He asked to see the restored Cave 16, known to be Wang’s ‘chief care’,81 as well as ‘the pride and the mainstay of his [Dunhuang] existence’.82 In a famous episode from his published accounts (not recorded in his diaries),83 Stein sought to win Wang’s trust by invoking the seventh-century Buddhist monk Xuanzang 玄奘:

en: The following day, 23 May 1907, Wang Yuanlu finally opened the door to Cave 17, which Stein depicted as a ‘black hole’ where ‘no examination of the manuscripts would be possible’.88 ItwasagreedthatWangwouldcontinuetotakeoutabundleortwoatatimeandallow them to ‘look rapidly through their contents in a less cramped and dark part of the temple precincts’.89 A small room in the antechapel of Cave 16, sheltered from view, was turned into an improvised ‘reading room’ for Stein and Jiang, who had to work quickly for fear that Wang might change his mind.90 Responsible for retrieving items, Wang Yuanlu began with the ‘miscellaneous’ bundles he had stacked atop the ‘regular’ bundles.91 Stein thus looked through a ‘large bundle of silk and cotton banners and prayer flags’, two Chinese bundles, ‘a large convolute of mixed papers’, and ‘one packet of large C[entral] A[sian] sheets’.92
zh: 次日，即1907年5月23日，王圆箓终于打开了第17窟的大门。斯坦因曾将那个地方描述为“黑洞”，称在那里“根本无法对写本进行任何检查”。双方约定，王圆箓每次会取出一两个卷束，让他们在寺庙中较为宽敞且光线较好的地方“快速浏览其内容”。第16窟前厅的一个小房间被临时改造成斯坦因和蒋孝琬的“阅览室”，他们必须抓紧时间工作，生怕王圆箓改变主意。负责取物的王圆箓首先处理的是那些堆放在“常规”卷束之上的“杂项”卷束。于是斯坦因便查看了一“大卷由丝绸、棉布旗帜及经幡构成的物品”，两卷中国式的卷束，“一大叠混杂的纸张”，以及“一包较大的中亚纸张”。

zh: 各种许愿物、各类纸张……由于形状不规则且固定方式不同，很容易与那些装着汉文和藏文佛教经典卷的规整包袋区分开来。幸运的是，恰恰因为这些物品形状极不规则，道士在堆砌我称之为“图书馆卷束”的墙状阵列时才将它们置于最上层。（182–3）他认为，王氏曾将几组这样的卷束放置在洞穴的最底部，“以便把低矮的泥台变成平坦的基面”。

en: Stein considered these questions. Regarding the first, he concluded that Wang had replaced the material in a different order: ‘The utter confusion prevailing in these bundles and their careless fastening, often without an outer cloth cover, clearly showed that no trouble had been taken to preserve the materials in whatever kind of arrangement they might have originally been found’12 (1921: 811). He noted that the ‘miscellaneous bundles’ were on top and concluded that Wang had left these last when replacing material in the cave after his initial discovery and emptying of the cave.
zh: 斯坦因对这些问题进行了思考。针对第一个问题，他得出结论认为王是按不同的顺序重新摆放了这些材料：“这些卷束中存在的极度混乱状况，以及它们被草率地捆扎、往往还缺乏外层布套的事实，都清楚地表明，人们根本没有费心去按照这些材料最初被发现的那种排列方式来保存它们”12（1921：811）。他注意到“杂项卷束”位于最上方，因而推断王是在最初发现并清空洞窟之后，再次整理洞窟内的物品时才把它们留在了最后。
